title: Evaluating a Generate–Validate–Repair Pipeline for LLM‑based Network Configuration: A Paired, Emulation‑Grounded Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, emulation‑grounded experiment (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26) to test whether integrating a deterministic network verifier into a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline reduces the rate of unsafe configuration applications from a single hosted LLM relative to an LLM‑only pipeline. Under the registered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial LLM generation per task reused across both arms) we ran N=240 paired intent→configuration tasks (144 in‑distribution, 48 distribution‑shift, 48 adversarial). All archived analysis artifacts report every paired episode as safe under both arms (baseline successes = 240/240; guarded successes = 240/240). The preregistered primary estimand—the absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate (guarded − baseline)—is 0.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical shared candidates that passed deterministic validation in every task, no validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair_attempts = 0) and the paired contrast is degenerate. We report the preregistered design, exact artifact‑grounded mapping to archived outputs, an evidence‑based failure analysis explaining the null paired outcome, and concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for future informative GVR evaluations.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation while preserving multi‑device ordering, dependency, and invariants is a core NetOps challenge. Language‑model‑driven NetOps agents can produce plausible textual outputs that nonetheless violate execution semantics (ordering, transient invariants, protected‑resource touches). Emulation‑grounded closed‑loop evaluation—applying generated configs to device images or simulators and deterministically scoring outcomes—reveals such semantic failures [1]. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines pair LLM generation with a deterministic verifier and optional automated repair; this pattern aims to convert textual plausibility into execution safety by catching and correcting semantic violations before application [2,3].

Despite prior reports of repair gains on synthetic and semi‑synthetic faults, open empirical questions remain about verifier benefit under distribution shift and adversarial prompts and about paired experimental designs that can detect verifier causal effects. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the exact estimand: the absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate (guarded − baseline). The study preserves per‑call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts so every numeric claim below maps directly to archived evidence. We emphasize that, under the executed semantics, the guarded arm can alter a pair’s final outcome only by (a) failing validation on the shared initial candidate or (b) applying a validator‑triggered repair.
sections.related_work:
Executable, emulation‑grounded benchmarks place LLM agents into realistic control loops and have demonstrated that many failures are semantic and operational rather than purely textual; NetConfArena exemplifies this approach and motivates closed‑loop scoring [1]. Across program and configuration repair literature, generate–validate architectures recur: deterministic/static validators frequently enable high repair coverage for many syntactic and local semantic faults, but full semantic coverage remains a challenge and depends on verifier design and specification completeness [2,4,6]. Surveys of agentic LLM architectures and evaluation practices identify tool augmentation, verifier integration, and uncertainty calibration as promising patterns for operational safety, while noting that evaluations are often benchmark‑bound and that external validity is limited [3,5].

Our study is distinguished by a predeclared paired estimand, explicit shared_initial_candidate preregistration semantics, deterministic emulation scoring, and full archival of per‑call and analysis artifacts. These features make the measured estimand and its null outcome directly reconcilable to the archived execution manifest and analysis outputs.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired difference in unsafe_apply rate: guarded minus baseline). The archived analysis executor reports 'success' as the safe outcome; archived condition_summary.csv shows baseline_success_count = 240 and guarded_success_count = 240, mapping directly to the estimand and implying baseline_unsafe_apply_count = 0 and guarded_unsafe_apply_count = 0.

Design and execution contract: The preregistered design is paired with shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one LLM generation per task was produced and reused across both arms; guarded episodes could request up to one validator‑triggered repair. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm adherence: planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, complete_pair_count = 240, hosted_model_call_event_count = 240, model_calls_used = 240, and provider_call_audit.stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 240. The declared model in the archived model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini. The deterministic verifier used by the guarded pipeline was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; repair_attempts are recorded in the repair logs (repair_attempts = 0).

Tasks and sampling: N = 240 paired tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and blocked into topology/vendor clusters: in‑distribution 60% (144), distribution‑shift 20% (48), adversarial 20% (48). Per the preregistration, verifier PASS vs emulator outcomes would be cross‑checked and flagged as 'possible false‑safe' for sensitivity analyses; none were detected in this run (contamination_summary.csv empty).

Scoring and analysis: Binary final outcome per task: safe (0) or unsafe (1), determined by deterministic emulation and validator/simulator checks. The primary analysis was executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 and produced the paired contingency table (n11 = 240; n10 = 0; n01 = 0; n00 = 0), estimate = 0.0, paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All analysis artifacts and logs are archived (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The preregistered power plan targeted detectability of an absolute 8 percentage‑point reduction (alpha = 0.05, target power >80%) under anticipated baseline rates; realized baseline_success_rate = 1.0 makes that planned sensitivity moot for this run and is discussed below.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: The run completed per plan: planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, complete_pair_count = 240. Provider call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 240, cache_miss_count = 240, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 240, confirming one shared initial generation per task and no cross‑condition independent generations.

Primary outcomes and contingency: All paired episodes were scored safe in both arms. analysis/condition_summary.csv records baseline successes = 240, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 240, guarded failures = 0. The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 240, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired estimator (guarded_unsafe_rate − baseline_unsafe_rate) = 0.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. These results and the supporting CSVs are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.

Validator and repair activity: Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 validated every shared initial candidate (validation_before.valid = true and validation_after.valid = true in per‑task validator_trace entries). No validator‑triggered repairs were invoked (repair_provider_trace_path = null across episodes; repair_attempts = 0). Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000004-*.json) show validation_before and validation_after snapshots with validator_pass semantics and violation_count = 0.

Unused sensitivity channels: The preregistered 'possible false‑safe' and infra‑failure channels were not exercised (contamination_summary.csv empty; missingness_summary.csv indicates no infra failures or unscorable episodes). Subgroup slices (in‑distribution, shift, adversarial) are degenerate (all zeros) in the archived subgroup contingency exports.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded explanation for the null paired contrast: Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics both arms began from the identical single LLM candidate per task. The guarded arm can only change the final paired outcome by (a) failing deterministic validation of that shared candidate or (b) applying a validator‑triggered repair that yields a different final configuration. In this execution every shared initial candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and no repairs were invoked (provider_call_audit and validator_trace fields confirm this). Consequently the guarded and baseline final configurations were identical for every task and the paired contingency is degenerate (n_11 = 240; no discordant pairs), producing estimate = 0.0, CI = [0.0,0.0], p = 1.0.

Design tradeoffs and implications: Shared_initial_candidate semantics enforces a tight, model‑call‑efficient pairing (one generator sample per task), but it also suppresses generator variability between arms; empirical detection of a verifier causal effect therefore requires that initial candidates sometimes fail the verifier or that repairs are applied. In practical terms, to obtain informative paired contrasts future studies should (explicitly per preregistered alternatives): (A) permit independent initial generations per arm so the verifier intervenes on a broader set of generator outputs; (B) increase adversary strength or diversify adversarial protocols to induce more validator failures; or (C) expand repair budgets (multiple repair iterations) and instrument repair traces to study repair search dynamics. These recommendations are motivated directly by archived provider_call_audit and repair logs showing shared_initial_generation = 240 and repair_attempts = 0.

Statistical and inference note: The preregistered power plan assumed a nonzero baseline unsafe rate and targeted an absolute 8 percentage‑point detectable reduction with N=240 pairs. Realized baseline success_rate = 1.0 (no unsafe applies) eliminates discordant pairs and precludes detecting verifier benefit under the current semantics; this is not a failure of analysis execution but an expected statistical consequence of the observed data and the preregistered design choices. Future designs that seek to measure verifier causal effects should ensure generator variability or adversary strength sufficient to produce informative discordant pairs.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity is limited by the shared_initial_candidate contract (explicit and archived). Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s finite check set; validator traces record observed_touched_field_count and violation_codes, but unmodeled semantic fault classes may still exist. External validity is limited: tasks derive from a NetConfArena‑style synthetic emulation corpus (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and do not fully represent production multi‑vendor idiosyncrasies. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency prevents inferences about verifier benefit in other execution regimes; archived artifacts permit reproducible sensitivity re‑executions under alternative generation semantics.

Operational implications and concrete next steps: For practitioners evaluating GVR pipelines with paired designs, we recommend (1) choosing generation semantics aligned to the causal estimand (avoid shared_initial_candidate if the goal is to measure verifier benefit across generator variability), (2) using adversary ensembles and stronger perturbations to stress verifiers, (3) expanding repair budgets and logging repair search behavior, and (4) improving verifier semantic coverage and routinely cross‑checking validator PASS against emulator outcomes to detect false‑safe cases. The archived execution and analysis artifacts provide the necessary instrumentation to implement and evaluate these changes reproducibly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired, emulation‑grounded evaluation of a GVR pipeline for LLM‑based network configuration under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Observed outcome: every paired episode was safe under both arms, yielding a paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0). This null paired contrast is artifact‑grounded: a single shared initial LLM candidate per task was validated successfully by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in every case, and no validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair_attempts = 0); therefore the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to create discordant outcomes. Our archived execution, validator traces, and analysis artifacts (preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0d..., bootstrap_seed: 1729, bootstrap_resamples: 10000, model_calls_used: 240, planned_episode_count: 480, completed_episode_count: 480) substantiate these conclusions and inform concrete recommendations for future experimental designs that can produce informative paired contrasts by altering generation semantics, adversary strength, or repair budgets.

disclosure_statement: Models and orchestration: Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini via the registered adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and permitted up to one validator‑triggered repair per task. Preregistration and autonomy: the study was preregistered (study id study-cand-1-gvr-verifier-adversarial-2026-08-01; preregistration SHA‑256: 3e73ca0dc935a8754bf2dfbe6869ff989c47f1db0d93e2ca34809be8ebf95e26) and executed under the frozen plan after the autonomy lock. Human role and autonomy boundary: prior to the autonomy lock the human Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt; all literature search, experiment design, preregistration, execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock per the track rules. Generation semantics and causal constraint: the registered adapter used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one shared initial generation per task reused across both arms); therefore, under this contract, only validator failures of the shared candidate or validator‑triggered repairs could create paired divergences. Execution accounting (archived): planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, complete_pair_count = 240, hosted_model_call_event_count = 240, model_calls_used = 240. Immutable master prompt: the initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). No manual human editing of the technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Emulator and corpus scope: tasks used a NetConfArena‑style synthetic emulation corpus; external validity to production, multi‑vendor networks and operator workflows is limited.
Single model: a single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) was tested; results do not imply generality across models, prompts, or prompting strategies.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired design used one shared initial generation per task; this prevents generator variability between arms and makes verifier benefit contingent on initial candidate failures.
Adversary bounds: adversarial prompts were generated under a preregistered, fixed adversary protocol and do not represent unconstrained, adaptive adversaries.

Verifier coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements a finite set of checks; uncovered semantic fault classes may remain undetected by the verifier, and verifier PASS vs simulator outcome mismatches were planned to be flagged and analyzed (none occurred in this run).
